plan.title: Labs 7 and 10 start with zsh-only preflight despite later Windows routes

narratives.Description: Labs 7 and 10 currently present a zsh-only Environment gate even though each page later offers a Native Windows PowerShell route, forcing Windows learners to scan past ordered tasks before they can validate their starting state. This story adds platform branches at both gates and locks their structure with focused verifiers while preserving the later routes as candidate whole-lab paths and the course's environment-blocked stop.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md` and `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md` so each Environment section branches before state creation and the Windows branch covers tool checks, helper path, `create`, and guard behavior.
2. Clarify in both lab pages how the compressed Native Windows route relates to the ordered tasks without promoting that route to a verified platform path.
3. Extend `scripts/verify-module-7.mjs`, `scripts/verify-module-10.mjs`, and their focused test files so a zsh-only regression, missing Windows starting-state operation, or lost route-status wording fails deterministically.
narratives.UserStory: As a Windows learner, I want Labs 7 and 10 to present a PowerShell starting-state branch at the environment gate, so that I can validate my platform before following the ordered lab.
narratives.Traces: Accepted bound remedy on https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/issues/60#issuecomment-5786102665, independently audited in comment 5787642826 and confirmed by synthesis comment 5787726505; relieves recorded pain P1.
narratives.Overview:
## Learner context

Independent Windows/PowerShell pilot of the required 0.119.5 course path.

## Problem

Both required labs later provide a native Windows/PowerShell route, but their primary **Environment and starting-state check** instructs every learner to use a dedicated zsh terminal:

- `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md`: “Use a dedicated zsh terminal...”
- `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md`: “Use a dedicated zsh terminal...”

The Windows routes do not appear until much later in each page. This contradicts the course prerequisite that Windows with PowerShell 7.4+ is a candidate learner platform.

## Pain experienced

At the gate where I must decide whether I have a valid environment, the page tells me to switch to a shell that is not the selected platform. I have to scan ahead past the ordered lab tasks to discover whether Windows is supported and which checks replace the zsh block. That undermines the starting-state gate and makes “complete every step in order” ambiguous.

## Proposed fix

At the start of each environment section, branch explicitly:

- macOS/zsh and Linux/bash: link to the existing shell block;
- Windows/PowerShell 7.4+: link to or place the full native preflight block there.

Keep platform status clear, but do not make a Windows learner pass through a zsh-only instruction before reaching the documented Windows route.

No Directive source or framework internals were consulted.

Open critique of the Labs 7 and 10 starting-state recut. Re-verified at dispatch SHA `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e` with `git show <sha>:path` (no `origin/master` fetch). Stop 1 line cites matched. Helpers already accept `win32`; the page-level starting-state identity is the defect.

## 1. The late Windows sections are whole-lab scripts, not a starting-state preflight

blocks-the-design

Evidence. Both environment headings instruct a dedicated zsh terminal, then a `sh` create/guard/install block (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:49-87`, `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:38-71`). The only Windows blocks are late headings `## Native Windows PowerShell 7.4+ route` (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:412`, `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:277`). Lab 7's route "covers starting state, execution, acceptance, fresh reset, and recoverable archive" and runs `create`, `guard`, `install`, `run --intent=implement`, authored verify, `reset`, and `archive` in one script (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:414-457`). Lab 10's route runs `create` through `archive` and tells the learner to edit `src/greeting.mjs` "as specified in the implementation step" (`labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:279-305`, comment at `:294`). That implementation spec lives in Task 2 (`labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:134-145`). Lab 7's `run --intent=implement` is the helper's automated lifecycle (`lifecycle-lab.mjs` `runLifecycle`), which is Tasks 1-4 compressed, not the environment create/guard/install gate.

Failure mode. Binding "link to or place the full native preflight block" at each environment section treats those late headings as the Windows starting-state check. A link sends a Windows learner into a whole-lab script before Tasks 1-N. Placing that script at the starting-state gate double-runs `create` if the learner then follows the ordered tasks. The two labs are not the same substitute: Lab 7's script replaces the observation tasks; Lab 10's script still needs Task 2 in the zsh-ordered body. "Complete every step in order" stays undefined.

Disposition. The recut cannot bind that proposed fix as written. Split two artifacts per lab: (1) Windows starting-state checks at the environment heading (tools, helper path, create, guard, and Lab 7/10's `.bin` vs `dist/bin.js` launcher note at `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:461`); (2) the existing compressed route as a candidate whole-lab path. For each lab, state whether (2) replaces the ordered tasks or the learner still walks Tasks 1-N. Until that split exists, the environment-section branch has no safe Windows target.

## 2. Reuse the course's starting-state branch and the environment-blocked stop

sharpens-framing

Evidence. Lab 2 already branches inside Environment and starting-state check: `### macOS/zsh — verified locally; Linux/bash — candidate` and `### Windows/PowerShell 7.4+ — candidate pending native evidence` (`labs/02-disposable-initialization.md:86`, `:148`). Lab 5 names both shells at the environment heading, then gives a Windows block beside the first create (`labs/05-projection-drift-recovery.md:41-87`). Capstone uses `### macOS and Linux` then `### Windows PowerShell 7.4+` under the same heading (`labs/capstone-end-to-end.md:59-120`). `labs/README.md:64-65` and `:128` require the exact block for the learner's shell and separate commands when PowerShell syntax differs. Course map already allows an unverified Lab 7/10/11 environment to stop as environment-blocked rather than treat a candidate platform as verified (`curriculum/README.md:176-179`). Both lab records already mark Windows as unverified (`labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:9,14,18-19`; `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:9,14,18-19`). Helpers record `nativeClaim: candidate` off Darwin (`lifecycle-lab.mjs:360`).

Failure mode. A new jump-link to the late route, or an early Windows branch that only "keeps platform status clear," invites executing the unverified compressed script as the 0.119.5 complete lab. That collides with the course-map stop and with Lab 2's candidate heading, which is the existing authoring pattern.

Disposition. The lean can bind as a starting-state discoverability recut if it reuses Lab 2/5/capstone environment-section branching, keeps the Lab 2 candidate heading text, and keeps `curriculum/README.md:176-179` as an allowed stop. Do not add a third pattern. Do not promote the compressed route to verified preflight.

## 3. Adjacent zsh-only starts stay on Lab 11 and Module 10

footnote

Lab 11 uses a `sh` create at Environment and starting-state check and the same late Native Windows heading (`labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md:28-40`, `:270`). Module 10's prerequisite table still requires "a dedicated zsh terminal" (`curriculum/modules/10-implementation-golden-path.md:12`); Module 7's table says "a dedicated terminal" (`curriculum/modules/07-scope-lifecycle.md:12`). Out of this issue's Labs 7 and 10 identity; leftover if the bound recut is lab pages only.

## Road-not-taken

Considered moving the Native Windows headings to sit under each environment section with no other change. Rejected because those scripts still run the whole lab, and Lab 10 still depends on Task 2. What would flip that: split each Windows section into a starting-state PowerShell create/guard/install block plus a later task-body route, matching Lab 5.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected reading: a top-of-section link is enough discoverability, and Windows learners never needed the ordered zsh tasks. That holds only if the recut states that the compressed route replaces Tasks 1-N for Windows, and if Lab 10 duplicates or fragment-links the Task 2 greeting spec. The issue text still treats the late block as preflight and still names ordered-step ambiguity, so that reading does not bind as written.

## 1. Reading harvest item 1 as an addendum after the zsh lead

footnote
